source.title: Further Advantages of Data Augmentation on Convolutional Neural Networks

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Its own results refine V5 by comparing true-label test performance with weight decay and dropout enabled versus disabled across training-set sizes and All-CNN depths; it does not test random-label fitting.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses Zhang et al.'s random-label findings as prior work, but does not run random-label experiments. Its results on true-label generalization with explicit regularizers removed bear on the second part of V5. Values in Figures 1 and 2 are not transcribed in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study extends V5's true-label generalization clause to reduced training sets and changed network depths using its own regularizer ablations. It does not test random-label fitting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. With sufficient augmentation, removing weight decay and dropout preserves or improves generalization when training-set size or architecture changes. The authors hypothesize that transferred regularization hyperparameters cause the poorer regularized performance; they do not demonstrate this through retuning experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares explicit regularization and data augmentation on true-label image classification; it does not apply the original random-label intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with training-set size, architecture, and explicit-regularizer setting; one stated exception is WRN on 50% of CIFAR-10.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks (ICANN) 2018
record.problems: The supplied text gives qualitative summaries but not the plotted accuracy values. Results use CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 convolutional networks and do not test fitting random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure-level comparisons are recorded as aggregates where the prose does not supply individual plotted values.

untested.parts: Random-label training error, chance test performance, and fitting without architecture or hyperparameter changes.
Relative fitting time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training fit and test degradation across label-corruption fractions.
Whether regularizers prevent fitting random labels; whether removing data augmentation preserves true-label generalization. The clearest reported support retains heavier augmentation.
The temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: These findings support only V5's true-label clause. Regularized baselines retain their original hyperparameters, so the comparisons do not establish superiority over newly tuned regularized models. Figure accuracies are unavailable in the supplied text, but its explicit qualitative comparisons support the verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random training labels, training error, test error, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled, permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across increasing fractions of corrupted labels.

Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels. The study tests only true-label generalization with weight decay and dropout removed, in experiments that still use data augmentation.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.

rows.subject: All-CNN
rows.size_stated: Original, shallower (9 layers, 374 K parameters), and deeper (15 layers, 2.4 M parameters) versions; original has 12 layers and about 1.3 M parameters.
rows.operation_detail: Compared true-label test performance with weight decay and dropout versus no explicit regularization, using reduced training sets and data augmentation.
rows.baseline: Models trained with weight decay and dropout; figure values not stated in text.
rows.value: Models without explicit regularization generally outperform regularized counterparts; for WRN on 50% of CIFAR-10, the regularized model is marginally better (< 0.001).
rows.note: The prose describes the overall comparison and exception, but the figure's individual values are not given. It discusses All-CNN and WRN; this row records the reported aggregate comparison rather than separate model values.
rows.check: The row combines All-CNN and WRN despite naming only All-CNN. The shallower/deeper architectures belong to R2, not this reduced-data comparison. Split by model, dataset and training-set fraction. Under heavier augmentation, removing weight decay and dropout improves accuracy except for WRN on 50% of CIFAR-10, where the reported disadvantage is below 0.001. All reported test accuracies average predictions over 10 light test-time augmentations.

source_check.correct: The aggregate comparison covers original All-CNN and WRN-28-10. Shallower and deeper All-CNN variants belong to the architecture comparison in Section 3.2. Under heavier augmentation, removal generally improves accuracy; WRN on 50% of CIFAR-10 instead has a marginal regularization advantage (< 0.001).
source_check.problem: The subject names only All-CNN and includes depth variants, while the reported reduced-data comparison covers All-CNN and WRN.

rows.subject: All-CNN
rows.size_stated: Original (12 layers, about 1.3 M parameters), shallower (9 layers, 374 K parameters), and deeper (15 layers, 2.4 M parameters).
rows.operation_detail: Compared true-label test performance with weight decay and dropout versus no explicit regularization across All-CNN depths, using data augmentation.
rows.baseline: All-CNN trained with weight decay and dropout; figure values not stated in text.
rows.value: Without explicit regularization, the deeper architecture improves on the original on both datasets and the shallower architecture has a slight performance drop; regularized models have much worse performance, with a dramatic drop for deeper architectures.
rows.note: The prose reports qualitative comparisons; exact accuracies and augmentation-level values are not stated.
rows.check: The qualitative comparison is supported, but aggregates architecture, dataset and augmentation conditions. Split those conditions where figure values are available. The slight decline for shallower unregularized networks is relative to original depth, not evidence that removing regularizers harms generalization. Exact accuracies cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

relationships.condition: All-CNN and WRN on reduced CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training sets with heavier augmentation
relationships.reason: R1 reports improved accuracy after removing weight decay and dropout, with only a below-0.001 disadvantage for WRN on 50% of CIFAR-10; removal therefore does not itself make generalization poor.
relationships.display_finding: Removing weight decay and dropout improved accuracy except for a disadvantage below 0.001 for WRN using 50% of CIFAR-10.
